This is NPR News Now. The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington. I'm Corva Coleman. NPR has learned that the U.S. brought
home all its long-range bomber planes from a base in the U.K. last week. That was because
of a credible threat linked to Iran. NPR's Greg Myrie says it's according to a U.S. official,
not authorized to speak publicly. This threat potentially involved a drone attack. The U.S.
planes were flown out Sunday. They've returned to home bases in the U.S. And these are long-range
bombers that were part of a larger contingent of U.S. war planes that used this British base in
recent months to carry out airstrikes in Iran. NPR's Greg Myrie reporting the potential threat
came to light after the U.K. arrested five men in vans last week near the U.K. air base. Two more
men were arrested a few days later. Most of them have been released on bail. No one has been
charged. The Trump administration is urging Russia to be more transparent about the death of a lab
worker in Siberia last week. The case is suspected to be pneumatic plague. NPR's Michelle Kellerman
reports the State Department says it's been in touch with Russia's foreign ministry since the
news first emerged last Friday. Secretary of State Marco Rubio sounded frustrated with the lack of
information, but he wouldn't speculate when asked whether this could have been a leak of a strain
of the plague that was altered by Russia. I think it's incumbent upon Russia to obviously share more
information with the world. That's what they should do. That's what we hope they will do.
And the more we can learn about what happened, the better all of us can be in a position of
responding. So far, it is State Department health experts who have been reaching out to Russia for
information, though arms control experts have expressed concern that Russia maintains an
offensive biological warfare program. Michelle Kellerman, NPR News, the State Department. The
Tennessee woman who survived a failed execution last week is now awake. Her attorneys are expected
in court today for a hearing. From member station WPLN, Katherine Sweeney has more.
Krista Pike has been hospitalized since Wednesday. That's when Tennessee tried and failed to put her
to death for her role in the 1995 killing of Colleen Slimmer. The prison administered two
doses of lethal drugs, but she ultimately left in an ambulance. Her attorneys announced Tuesday
afternoon she was not only conscious, but speaking. They said she was handcuffed to her bed,
even though her arms are covered and burns and blisters. They attribute those injuries
to bad IV placement during her attempted execution and say it's likely the Pinto
Barbatol intended to kill her flowed into her flesh instead of into her bloodstream.
For NPR News, I'm Katherine Sweeney in Nashville. This year's Nobel Prize in Chemistry has been
awarded to two scientists. Henri Kagan and Kenzo Soai are being honored by the Nobel
Committee for Work that contributes to foundational chemistry. You're listening to NPR News from
Washington. The two main candidates running for governor of Michigan faced off in a debate last
night. The event was carried by News Nation. From Michigan Public Radio, Colin Jackson reports
Republican John James and Democrat Jocelyn Benson traded criticism over President Trump.
From the beginning to the end of the debate, Michigan Democratic nominee for governor
Jocelyn Benson tried to tie her Republican opponent to unpopular Trump administration
policies. If you like gas pushing $5 a gallon or mortgage rates over 7% or terrorist taxing just
about everything we pay for, then John James is your guy. But James often said he disagreed
with Trump, especially on issues like the war in Iran and the trade war with Canada.
I've actually called out the administration specifically talking with the trade ambassador
and saying that we must get back to the table, stop acting like children, and negotiate
for reciprocal, fair, and mutually beneficial arrangement. Absentee voting in the race has
already begun. For NPR News, I'm Colin Jackson in Grand Rapids, Michigan. The National Hurricane
Center says tropical storm Isaias has formed in the Gulf of Mexico. It's nearly 600 miles
south of the mouth of the Mississippi River and its top sustained winds are at 40 miles per hour.
Tropical storm Isaias is expected to pick up strength rapidly. Forecasters are warning
it could be a significant hurricane when it reaches the U.S. coast in a few days.
Oscar-winning actress Eva Marie Saint has died at the age of 102. She played memorable roles in
films such as "On the Waterfront" for which she won an Oscar. I'm Corva Kuhlman, NPR News, in Washington.
